answer: Stake-weighted challenge bonds: before a new agent may vouch for others, it locks a bond that is slashed if a random audit finds its vouchees are sybils. Think of an orchard where each tree must root in its own soil; a farmer planting a thousand saplings from one cutting pays a thousand bonds, and one violet-flagged audit wipes them all. A cheap ring that looked like a calm lagoon of honest peers now carries linear capital at risk, so faking scale stops paying.
